To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the interfacial forces between two surfaces can affect their (electro)-chemical properties, and that the (electro)-chemistry of the surfaces can affect their interfacial forces, as well as the properties of the intervening electrolyte solution.

(1) the surface forces apparatus combined with electrochemical attachments allows for simultaneous measurements of interfacial energies and electrochemical reactions, (2) the electrochemical reactions and surface interactions are strongly coupled and can affect each other, and (3) the electrochemical attachment allows for the chemical reaction to be unambigously determined.

(1) the electrostatic interactions between charged surfaces can be used to control their (electrochemical) reactions, (2) the electrostatic forces between surfaces can affect their chemical reactivity, and (3) the chemical reactions can affect the surface forces and surface-surface interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the interplay of physical interactions, electrochemical reactions, and the structure and dynamics of the interfacial region in electrolytes, which are important to many areas of chemistry, biology, materials science, and engineering.
the interplay of interfacial electrochemical forces and reactions, and how the two influence each other.
the fundamental question of the relationship between the physical forces and energies of interaction between extended surfaces immersed in solution, and their electrochemical reactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interfacial forces are important for the chemistry at the interface and that the chemistry at the interfacial region is important for the interfacial force.
the interplay of electrochemistry and surface forces in the nanometer scale is a very active field of research with many open questions and challenges.
electrochemistry and interfacial forces go together, hand-in-hand.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interfacial forces are not only a consequence of the electrochemical reactions, but they can also affect the electrochemical reactions and vice versa.
the interfacial forces between surfaces can be used to control and/or measure the electrochemistry at these interfaces.
the electrochemical reactions of two surfaces are affected by their interaction forces and energies, which are in turn affected by their chemical reactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the interfacial forces can be used to control the chemical reactions, and the reactions can in turn be used to control interfacial forces, which is of importance to many applications, such as the development of nanodevices, biosensors, and energy storage devices.

the interplay of surface forces and electrochemical processes is an important and underappreciated area of research that has great potential for further advances in many scientific and technological areas.
